samples.summary: backendErrorEnvelope silently discards non-`{error:{…}}` backend bodies, losing the server's message (Nest default error shape)
samples.evidence: `const raw = data?.error; const fields = raw && typeof raw === 'object' && !Array.isArray(raw) ? {...raw} : {}` (formatter.ts:99-103). NestJS's default HttpException body is `{"statusCode":404,"message":"Document not found","error":"Not Found"}` — `error` is a STRING, so `fields` becomes `{}` and the emitted envelope is only `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}`. No global exception filter shaping `{error:{code,message}}` exists in packages/backend/src (grep for `ExceptionFilter` returned nothing; only hand-written bodies like TYPE_MISMATCH_BODY in docs-content.controller.ts:42 use that shape). Before this change every call site printed `JSON.stringify(res.data ?? …)` verbatim, so the user saw `message`. Now the actual failure reason is dropped on the most common backend error shape, across files/upload.ts:229, files/download.ts:64, docs/import.ts:178/215/238, notes/import.ts:168/201/220, slides/import.ts:197/247/268. Also note docs.ts:267 / notes.ts:150 / slides.ts:156 gate on `if (body?.error)`, which is truthy for the string `"Bad Request"`, so that branch is taken and the detail is lost rather than falling through.

samples.summary: CLI unconditionally requires a `state` echo the backend may not send — login then hangs 30s and fails with an unrelated timeout message
samples.evidence: login.ts:206 rejects any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, but the backend only appends it conditionally: `const stateEcho = state.nonce ? \`&state=…\` : ''` (auth.controller.ts:130). `state.nonce` is undefined whenever GitHubAuthGuard dropped it — non-string (duplicate `?nonce=a&nonce=b` makes express give an array), empty, or >128 chars (github-auth.guard.ts:34-38) — and, more importantly, whenever the CLI runs against a deployed backend that predates this change. In all those cases the genuine callback is answered with HTTP 400 'Invalid state', the promise never settles, and the user waits the full 30s for 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.' — a message that gives no hint of the real cause. There is no negotiation, version check, or diagnostic for the nonce-absent case.

samples.summary: Download failure envelope reports `HTTP 200` when the response succeeded but carried no bytes
samples.evidence: `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)` (download.ts:62) then emits `backendErrorEnvelope(res.data, { code: 'HTTP_ERROR', message: \`HTTP ${res.status}\` }, command)`. On the `res.ok && !res.bytes` branch `res.status` is 200 and `res.data` is undefined (http-client.ts:269-276 sets `data` only on the failure paths), so stderr reads `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 200"}}` — a self-contradictory diagnostic for an empty-body download. The previous code printed the generic `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}`, which at least did not assert a success status.

samples.summary: runCli mutates the caller-supplied program by registering a preAction hook on every invocation
samples.evidence: `program.hook('preAction', …)` at cli.ts:61 runs inside `runCli`, whose `program` parameter defaults to a fresh program but is explicitly designed to accept a caller-built one (tests do). Calling `runCli(sameProgram, …)` twice registers a second hook; every previously-registered closure still fires on later parses, keeping stale `Command` references alive and doing redundant work. Harmless today because each closure writes only its own `acting`, but it is an unbounded accumulation on a shared object rather than a per-run registration.

NestJS's default HttpException body is `{"statusCode":404,"message":"Document not found","error":"Not Found"}` — `error` is a STRING, so `fields` becomes `{}` and the emitted envelope is only `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}`. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. formatter.ts:99-103 only merges `data.error` when it is a non-array object; otherwise `fields = {}` and code/message fall back to the caller's generic `HTTP <status>` (lines 105-110). No global exception filter exists anywhere in the repo (repo-wide grep for ExceptionFilter/@Catch/useGlobalFilters/APP_FILTER returned nothing; main.ts registers no filter/interceptor), so Nest's default HttpException body `{statusCode, message, error:"Not Found"}` — where `error` is a STRING — is what the CLI receives. Backend paths the CLI hits throw plain Nest exceptions (document.service.ts:33, document.controller.ts:169/235/293/354/382, document-file.controller.ts:46/52, document-file-id.util.ts:54/60), so on a real 404/400 the server's `message` ("Document not found", "No documents specified") is silently discarded across all call sites (files/upload.ts:229, files/download.ts:64, docs/import.ts:179/215/238, notes/import.ts:168/201/220, slides/import.ts:198/247/266). Additionally the `if (body?.error)` gate at commands/docs.ts:197/267, notes.ts and slides.ts is truthy for the string reason phrase, so the lossy branch is actively taken. This is in-lane error handling that mis-handles/loses failure information on a common real path; nothing guards it.

finding.summary: CLI unconditionally requires a `state` echo the backend may not send — login then hangs 30s and fails with an unrelated timeout message
finding.evidence: login.ts:206 rejects any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, but the backend only appends it conditionally: `const stateEcho = state.nonce ? \`&state=…\` : ''` (auth.controller.ts:130). `state.nonce` is undefined whenever GitHubAuthGuard dropped it — non-string (duplicate `?nonce=a&nonce=b` makes express give an array), empty, or >128 chars (github-auth.guard.ts:34-38) — and, more importantly, whenever the CLI runs against a deployed backend that predates this change. In all those cases the genuine callback is answered with HTTP 400 'Invalid state', the promise never settles, and the user waits the full 30s for 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.' — a message that gives no hint of the real cause. There is no negotiation, version check, or diagnostic for the nonce-absent case.

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed. login.ts:206 rejects any /callback whose `state` does not constant-time match the nonce and returns without settling `callbackPromise` (deliberately keeping the listener open, comment at 203-205), so the only remaining settle path is the 30s timer at login.ts:257-265 which rejects with 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.' — a message unrelated to the real cause. On the server, auth.controller.ts:130-135 makes the echo conditional (`state.nonce ? '&state=...' : ''`) and still issues a valid code and redirects to the CLI port, i.e. it knowingly emits a callback a compliant CLI can never accept, with no fail-fast. github-auth.guard.ts:34-38 drops the nonce silently for non-string (duplicate query param -> array), empty, or >128-char values, and cli-auth.store.ts:13,45-61 carries it as optional. The CLI's own nonce (login.ts:42,46) always satisfies the guard, so the drop branches need a crafted URL; but the version-skew case (new CLI against a backend lacking the echo) cannot be ruled out from the repo and yields a fully broken `wafflebase login` with a misleading diagnostic. No guard or caller elsewhere makes the missing-state redirect unreachable — the backend itself builds it — so no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / counterexample) applies, and an unsettled promise plus mis-reported failure on a core flow is squarely in the correctness lane.

mergedFrom.summary: The new "one line per error, with `command`" stderr invariant is broken by the sibling error paths that bypass `outputError`

finding.summary: Many stderr error-envelope emitters bypass `outputError`, so they still print pretty-printed multi-line JSON with no `command` — breaking the one-line/attributed contract this change documents and tests
finding.evidence: The diff makes `outputError` emit a single line with `command` and the test asserts `expect(raw).not.toContain('\n')` (test/output.test.ts:148). But error envelopes are also written directly on real failure paths, all with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` and no `command`: docs.ts:195 and docs.ts:255 (backend-shaped error on `docs content` / `docs export`), notes.ts:148, notes.ts:203, slides.ts:154, slides.ts:204, schema.ts:32 (`{"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND"...}}` for `wafflebase schema <unknown>`), files/upload.ts:217 and files/upload.ts:227 (`errorJson`), files/download.ts:57, docs/import.ts:164/194/211, notes/import.ts:159/188/212, slides/import.ts:194/237/254. A caller following docs/design/cli.md §9 ("Errors: a single JSON line on stderr ... command") with a line-delimited parser sees a multi-line, unattributed body for these — i.e. the very backend-error cases the feature is meant to attribute. The new tests only cover the `outputError` path, so nothing catches it.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present in the working tree. Every stderr error-envelope emitter the finding names routes through the shared, single-line helpers `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:75-114), which use un-indented `JSON.stringify` and append `command`. The two docs.ts sites (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:202-209 and :268-274) pass `commandPath(this)` into `backendErrorEnvelope`, as do notes.ts:155-161/:216-222, slides.ts:161-167/:218-224, schema.ts:40-46, files/upload.ts:216-234, files/download.ts:63-69, and the docs/notes/slides import orchestrators. A repo-wide grep for `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` under packages/cli/src finds it only on stdout result bodies and config/session/dry-run paths — never on a stderr error envelope. The claim that "the new tests only cover the outputError path" is also false: packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:463-534 is a dedicated end-to-end block for emitters that never reach `outputError`, asserting `raw` contains no newline and carries `command: 'docs.content'`.
